scenes.headline: How ZCode's fix keeps undo on your machine
scenes.sub: The v3.14.0 checkpoint, and what an open repository can prove.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Lemur! ZCode, a coding agent, was reported to build and upload snapshots of local repositories. Here's how the fix works, and what the release can prove.

scenes.label: The fix
scenes.text: Checkpoint and restore survived. v3.14.0 moved it into your own git repository: a hidden ref, scoped to the current workspace, with no boundary to cross.
scenes.say: The fix kept the feature. Checkpoint and restore now live in your own git repository, as a hidden ref scoped to the current workspace.

left.title: Reported: archive and upload
items: A snapshot of the workspace, built on the machine
Sent to the vendor's object storage
left.say: As reported, the old workflow archived the workspace and sent it to the vendor's storage. A workspace includes dot git: every version of every file.

right.title: v3.14.0: a local git checkpoint
items: Written into the repository you already have
A hidden ref, no visible branch or commit
right.say: The new version writes the snapshot into the repository you already have. Git's object store is content-addressed and deduplicated, and it's already there.

items.text: Point git at a temporary index
items.say: Point git at a temporary index file, so your real index is never touched.
Stage everything, but only under the current workspace's path.
Write that into a tree, and wrap the tree in a commit object.
Point a hidden ref at it. No user-visible branch, and no ordinary commit.

scenes.label: outbound-request scenarios listed in NOTICE.md, and no snapshot upload among them
scenes.note: the repo shows what the client does now, not what it did
scenes.say: The open repository answers what the client does now. Its notice file lists seventeen outbound-request scenarios, and a snapshot upload isn't one. The history isn't there: two commits.

scenes.text: Undo needs somewhere to keep the old state. Git already keeps it locally, with no boundary to cross.
scenes.say: Every agent that edits your files needs undo, and undo needs somewhere to keep the old state. Git already keeps it on your machine.

recap: Checkpoints now live in a hidden local git ref
A temporary index, scoped to the workspace
The open repo shows the present, not the past
scenes.say: To recap: undo moved into a hidden git ref, built from a temporary index, and the open repository shows the present, not the past.
